stem: A logistics company's application writes an ever-growing volume of shipment documents to a single storage location and wants that storage to grow automatically with no capacity to provision ahead of time and no resize operation ever required.

choices.text: Amazon EBS with Elastic Volumes used to resize as needed
Amazon EFS with Provisioned throughput mode
Amazon FSx for Lustre with a Scratch deployment

rationale: Amazon S3 has effectively unlimited object storage capacity with nothing to provision ahead of time, which matches a requirement for growth with no capacity planning and no resize ever needed. EBS Elastic Volumes let you resize a volume live, but a resize action is still a required step, and a volume is capped at 64 TiB in a single Availability Zone, unlike S3. EFS with Provisioned throughput mode still requires setting and later adjusting a specific throughput number as the workload changes, which is a form of ongoing capacity planning. FSx for Lustre in a Scratch deployment is meant for short-lived, non-replicated processing and does not durably retain data, so it is not the growing, persistent store this document archive needs.
